newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-PASSARELLA DENIES ROW, MATURANA APPEALS FOR SENSE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PASSARELLA DENIES ROW, MATURANA APPEALS FOR SENSE.

text.p: Daniel Passerella, Argentina's beleagured national team coach, denied on Friday that he had fallen out with the president of the country's soccer federation and said he would not resign.
Meanwhile, Francisco Maturana, coach of Argentina's next World Cup opponents Ecuador, made an appeal for the importance of the match to be kept in perspective.
His comments appeared to be aimed at avoiding the build up of a warlike atmosphere, following the unsavoury incidents which hit the South American qualifiers last week.
In Buenos Aires, Passarella dismissed as lies reports that he had been involved in a blazing row with Julio Grondona, president of the Argentine Football Federation.

Reports published on Thursday said the coach, known for his strong personality, had threatened to resign during the meeting. It was also reported that Grondona was fed up with the way Passarella had chopped and changed the squad.

"If they want me to go, they're going to have to get rid of me," Passarella said on Friday. "The meeting with Grondona was very relaxed. Anything else they say is a lie. There was no shouting, he gave me his full backing."

Passarella has been under fire since last Wednesday's debacle when Argentina lost 2-1 to Bolivia in La Paz, had two players sent off and were involved in a brawl that held up play for 10 minutes near the end.
Although the Bolivian team and police were fiercely criticised, Argentine public opinion was also angry at the national team's conduct.

Passarella was blamed for creating a bad atmosphere in the run-up to the game, storming out of a news conference the day before and offending the Bolivian nation by claiming it was inhuman to play in La Paz, at 3,600 metres above sea level.
Since returning to Argentina, Passarella, who during the game argued incessantly with officials on the touchline, has refused to talk.
"It's important that people remember that I haven't seen my family for a month," he said, adding: "I have nothing against the Bolivian people."

The defeat, the latest in a series of bad results in the competition, left Argentina fifth in the South American qualifying group and out of the qualifying places. The top four of the nine teams qualify for the finals in France.
Ecuador, who have never reached the finals and lead Argentina on goals scored, visit Buenos Aires on April 30 for another crucial game.
Maturana, their Colombian coach, seemed to have learned from Passarella's experiences when he tried to play down the importance of the match.
"As far as I understand, this is simply a match in which nobody's life is at stake. It is a game of football and there is no need to dramatise it," he said in Quito.
"It is no doubt an important game, just like all the other qualifiers, but we have to get rid of this life and death idea because I don't believe this is what football is about."

Last week's games were also marred by a brawl on the touchline during the Paraguay-Colombia clash in Asuncion. Three players were sent off and the media in both countries spent the next few days trading accusations.
